messages:
Maya: Heads-up — planning rollout of model-serving v2.3 to prod today at 16:00 PT. Canary (5%) for 10m then step to 50% if green. Including small observability changes (dashboard panel + a couple alert tweaks). Reply if you have schedule conflicts or objections.
Diego: I can monitor. Who's doing the actual deploy and who owns rollback?
Maya: Jacob will run the deploy. Diego + Lina will own the smoke & observability checks. I'll coordinate comms.
Jacob: I got this. Plan: kick at 16:00, verify canary within 10m, then manual ramp to 50% at ~16:15 if no issues. Rollback plan in case of failure: immediate rollback to v2.2 and abort ramp.
Jacob: Preflight checklist I'll follow:
```
# verify cluster health
kubectl get nodes && kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-server
# start canary
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/model-server model-server=redwood/model-server:v2.3-canary
# wait
kubectl -n inference rollout status deployment/model-server --watch
```
Lina: Observability notes — I'm pushing two commits in the monitoring repo:
- dashboard: add a "model_v2.3" panel (qps, p50/p95 latency, kv_cache_hit_rate)
- alerts: add temporary canary rule with a slightly relaxed p95 threshold and 3m for: to avoid noisy pages during warmup
I will also create a simple trace filter for quick root-cause: `service:model-server AND model_version:v2.3` so we can pull only canary traces.
Diego: For smoke I'll run the small generator script that hits the /generate endpoint with sample prompts and asserts responses. Quick command:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.prod/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"model-server:v2.3-canary","input":"Summarize: The quick brown fox"}' | jq '.text, .latency_ms'
```
I'll stream results into a small health log and alert if 5xx or p95 > 800ms for the canary.
Maya: Do we want to mute/disable pagerduty pages for non-critical alerts during the canary?
Lina: Yes — I'll mute the noisy latency pages for 30m while canary is running. I'll keep the critical error pages (5xx spikes, OOM) active. Mute command (monitoring UI): mute rule `model_high_latency` for 30m or use the API.
Jacob: Rollback commands if we need to revert quickly:
```bash
# kubectl rollback (if using k8s rollout history)
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/model-server
# or pin image back
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/model-server model-server=redwood/model-server:v2.2
```
Jacob: I'll also tag the canary with a short reason in the deploy bot: `deploy start v2.3 canary — maya/observability` so it's obvious in the audit log.
sre-bot: Scheduled deploy window recorded: deploy_id=deploy-1898804321, owner=Jacob, window=2026-03-17T16:00:00-07:00 PT, auto-rollout=false, rollback_cmd_hint='kubectl rollout undo'. Link to runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/deploy-model-server
Diego: I'll start the smoke runner at T+2m after canary image is live and post a short summary in this thread (p50/p95, any 5xx count).
Maya: Great. Lina, will you push the dashboard PR now so it's available to watch?
Lina: PR opened: https://git.internal/mon/repo/pulls/427 — dashboard panel and alert tweak included. I added description of intended temporary relax.
Jacob: All set from my side. I'll ping here 5m before starting and again when canary is up.
Maya: Thanks everyone — if no objections, proceeding with 16:00 PT. Please flag in-thread any unexpected findings during smoke. :thumbsup:
